statement: Pointwise decay for p<p_* together with finite-n continuity and monotonicity does not imply decay at p_*. For p_* in (0,1), 0<=p<=p_*, n>=1, f_n(p)=exp(-(p_*-p)n)/2 has those properties but f_n(p_*)=1/2.
assumptions: This is an abstract family of numbers, not claimed to arise from nearest-neighbour percolation.
source: Owner-own-work: w430 ATTEMPT.md independent checkpoint, saved before paired proof access
proof_or_counterexample: For fixed p<p_*, p_*-p>0 gives exponential decay; at p=p_* the exponent is zero. Parameter and radius monotonicity and continuity follow directly from the formula. The two iterated limits are 0 and 1/2.
remaining_gap: No implication of theta(p_c)>0 for the target model; no independent referee check yet.

statement: For nearest-neighbour Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d, every integer d>=2 and n>=1 satisfy P_(p_c)(0 connects to boundary Lambda_n)>=1/[2d p_c (2n+1)^(d-1)]. In particular no constants delta>0, C<infinity, c_0>0 bound these probabilities by C exp(-c_0 n) simultaneously for all n and p in (p_c-delta,p_c).
assumptions: Independent homogeneous Bernoulli bond percolation on nearest-neighbour Z^d
Lambda_n is the integer infinity-norm box
Duminil-Copin--Tassion Theorem 1.1 identifying the finite-set threshold with p_c
source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1502.03051, Theorem 1.1 and finite-set threshold definition; owner-own-work: w430 ATTEMPT.md independent deduction
proof_or_counterexample: Finite-set continuity and the threshold identity force phi_(p_c)(S)>=1. For S=Lambda_n each of its 2d(2n+1)^(d-1) boundary edges has an inside endpoint on the vertex boundary, so phi_(p_c)(Lambda_n)<=p_c 2d(2n+1)^(d-1) a_n(p_c). A uniform exponential estimate below p_c passes to p_c by continuity of finite-box events and contradicts this polynomial lower bound.
remaining_gap: No upper critical one-arm bound; theta(p_c)=0 remains unproved here. Independent referee check pending.

statement: Let d>=2, integer r>=0, and X in {0,1}^{Z^d} have independent sigma-fields on any two sets separated by infinity-norm distance greater than r. If P(X_x=0)<=64^(-4)/(r+1)^2 for every x, then P(0 belongs to an infinite nearest-neighbour good component)>0.
assumptions: Setwise sigma-field independence, not merely pairwise independence
Nearest-neighbour good components; no FKG or stationarity required
source: owner-own-work: w430 REVIEW_PACKET.md separately derived coarsening argument after auditing w429 L1-L4
proof_or_counterexample: On a coordinate plane, tile by squares of side r+1 and declare a coarse site good only if its whole tile is good. Failure <=(r+1)^2 delta by a union bound. Tile unions separated by coarse distance >1 have physical distance >=r+2, giving setwise 1-dependence. Four parity classes bound any m-site all-bad probability by epsilon^(m/4). A bad-star-circuit count <=m*8^m gives probability <=8/49 of an enclosing bad contour at epsilon=64^-4. The coarse origin is infinite with probability >=1-64^-4-8/49>0; adjacent fully good tiles yield a physical infinite component containing 0.
remaining_gap: Independent contour/quantifier check pending. No proof that hypothetical critical percolation provides compatible blocks satisfying this bound.

statement: For nearest-neighbour Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d, d>=2, with independently green vertices of density 1-exp(-h), let m_h(p)=P_(p,h)(C(0) meets green). For every h>0, q_h=p_c(1-m_h(p_c))<=p_c(1-theta(p_c)), and lim_(h down to 0) q_h=p_c(1-theta(p_c)). Thus q_h tends to p_c if and only if theta(p_c)=0.
assumptions: Independent green vertex marks independent of the bond configuration
source: Math-brain hit claim_c83c8a10ed54143e4ef3f372de021aed7fa80a9a7c8a05662da7b7c61b5a7615; primary https://arxiv.org/html/2304.12110 Theorem 2 and magnetization definition; owner-own-work w430 ATTEMPT.md deduction
proof_or_counterexample: m_h(p)=E_p[1-exp(-h |C(0)|)], with infinite cluster contributing one. Each m_h(p)>=theta(p); bounded convergence as h decreases to zero gives limit theta(p). Substitute p_c and multiply by positive p_c. Assuming q_h approaches criticality therefore assumes the target conclusion, rather than supplying a bridge.
